vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: karpathy-wiki-cn
Version: 1.1.1

The skill bundle implements a research knowledge management system based on the Karpathy LLM Wiki methodology. It includes a Python script (search-agent-papers.py) and a shell wrapper to search for and download academic papers from the legitimate arXiv API (export.arxiv.org). The instructions in SKILL.md are well-defined and strictly aligned with the stated purpose of maintaining a local markdown-based knowledge base, with no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's files, instructions, and bundled scripts are coherent with its stated purpose (building and maintaining a persisted Karpathy-style research wiki); it downloads papers from arXiv and writes/updates local wiki files, and it does not request unrelated credentials or mysterious network endpoints.

dimensions.detail: The name and description describe a persistent LLM-maintained wiki; the SKILL.md details ingest/query/lint workflows that involve saving raw sources, creating/updating markdown pages, and appending logs. The included scripts fetch recent arXiv papers into raw/papers, which directly supports the ingest step — nothing requested appears unrelated to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions limit activity to: reading provided materials, writing markdown under wiki/, saving sources under raw/, updating index.md and log.md, and optionally invoking local CLI tools. The instructions reference only local file paths and arXiv as an external source; they do not direct the agent to read unrelated system files or exfiltrate data to unexpected endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only) — lowest risk. Two bundled scripts implement the 'fetch arXiv PDFs' helper. The bash script calls the included Python script (expected), but the shell file also contains duplicated Python code after an exec line; that duplication is likely a sloppy concatenation and harmless because exec replaces the shell process, but it's weird and worth eyeballing before running.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths. Network use is limited to arXiv/export.arxiv.org and arxiv.org for PDF downloads, which aligns with its purpose. Optional tooling references (qmd, Marp, Dataview) are just recommendations and not required.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes and modifies files in the repository (raw/, wiki/, wiki/log.md, etc.) as part of normal operation. always:false (default) — it does not force inclusion. Allowing autonomous invocation means an agent could run these file writes/downloads without manual approval; this behavior is coherent with a persistent wiki but users should be aware the skill will create and modify files on disk.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: download recent arXiv papers and maintain a local markdown wiki. Before installing or enabling autonomous runs: 1) Inspect the two bundled scripts (search-agent-papers.py and the .sh) — the bash file contains duplicated Python content which is odd but probably harmless; remove or fix the duplicate if it bothers you. 2) Run the downloader script manually first in a safe directory to confirm behavior and to see disk usage and filenames. 3) Be aware the skill will write files to raw/ and wiki/ and append to wiki/log.md — back up any existing folders you care about. 4) Because the agent may be allowed to run autonomously, only enable that if you trust it to create and modify repo files and download PDFs. 5) If you don't want network downloads, do not grant the agent network access or disable the downloader. Overall this skill is internally consistent; exercise standard caution when allowing file system writes and network access.
